title.en: Exact cover packing with a real search

summary: Keep the search honest: a packing scene either runs a real backtracking search or replays a recorded one, and says which.
objective: Build a polycube packing puzzle whose solver explores placements as an exact cover search I can step, pause and inspect.
intent_signals: Show a packing puzzle being solved by an actual search.
Explain exact cover with cells that must be covered exactly once.
example_prompts: Build a polycube packing puzzle with a steppable exact cover search and a placement candidate list.
Show the search backtracking when a region becomes impossible to fill.
negative_signals: Not a claim of optimal or fastest solving; no benchmark is asserted.
Not a physics assembly: pieces do not slide, collide or fall.
not_for: Not a claim of optimal or fastest solving; no benchmark is asserted.
Not a physics assembly: pieces do not slide, collide or fall.

entities.name: Tray and cells
entities.guidance: Model the target volume as an explicit set of cells with coordinates, since exact cover is a statement about cells being covered once.

entities.name: Piece placements
entities.guidance: Enumerate placements as piece plus rotation plus offset and treat each as a candidate object, not as a transform applied to a mesh.

entities.name: Search view
entities.guidance: Show the current partial cover, the chosen branch and the depth, so backtracking is visible as retreat rather than as a jump.

state_contract.model: A cell set, a finite enumerated placement list (each piece under its allowed rotations at every in-bounds offset, with duplicate placements removed), a partial cover with a count per cell, and one piece-use element per supplied piece so that each piece is required exactly once alongside each cell being covered exactly once. Depth-first search with a declared branching rule ends in one of three outcomes: solution found, search exhausted with no solution, or paused at a declared step budget. Whether the run is live or a recorded replay is stated in the scene.
state_contract.authority: The cover counts are authoritative: a cell covered twice is a failure state, and no piece may be shown placed unless its cells are marked in the cover.
actions: Step the search forward one placement.
Run until the next complete solution.
Reset the tray, placements and search.
Run to exhaustion or to the declared step budget, and read which of the three outcomes ended the run.

invariants: A completed solution covers every cell exactly once and uses every supplied piece exactly once; a tiling that reuses one piece and omits another is rejected by the piece-use elements, not accepted as a cover.
Backtracking removes exactly the cells added by the placement being undone and restores that piece to the available set, so cover counts and piece availability always move together.
A solution count is a count of what this search found; it is a total only when the search reported exhaustion over the complete declared placement list, and never when it stopped at the step budget.
motion_guidance: Animate placement and removal so a backtrack is visible as the piece leaving, not as the scene resetting.
Keep step, pause and inspect available; a search that can only run to completion cannot be understood.
known_limits: Search cost grows sharply with tray size and piece symmetry; no interactive performance is promised.
Symmetric solutions may be counted more than once unless a symmetry-breaking rule is declared.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: Depth-first search for tiling-style problems can be implemented with reversible local operations on doubly linked lists so that every step affects the data incrementally, and adding a ghost element for each piece places the rule that each piece is used once on the same footing as the rule that each cell is covered once.
claims.scope: Technique described in the cited abstract, which was read in full while the paper body was not. The ghost element is exactly what makes each piece used once a covering rule alongside each cell covered once, which is why this recipe carries piece-use elements in its state.

object_craft.structure: A tray with visible cell divisions and open faces so partial fills are inspectable from outside.
object_craft.material: Neutral tray with a distinct treatment for uncovered cells, so remaining space is legible at a glance.
object_craft.articulation: The tray is static; only the cover state changes.

object_craft.structure: Polycubes built from unit cubes with slight bevels so seams are visible and piece shape is readable.
object_craft.material: Per-piece identity material kept constant across rotations, so a piece stays recognisable when reoriented.
object_craft.articulation: Placements snap to cell coordinates and are removed cleanly on backtrack.

physical_contract.scope: Discrete search with snapped placements; no contact, gravity or friction.
checks: No cell is covered more than once at any search step.
Backtracking restores the exact previous cover state.
